claims.claim_ar: نداء بـ «يا أهل الكتاب» كتحويل في مقام الخطاب (التفات) لانتقال المخاطَب من عموم الخطاب إلى مخاطبة مخصوصة لخلق تماس وحضور نفسي لدى المستمع.
claims.claim_en: The vocative particle يا in «يا أهل الكتاب» effects an iltifat (shift/turning) — moving from general discourse to a direct address to a specific addressee, creating immediacy and psychological engagement.
claims.rhetorical_effect: directs attention to the addressees, increases urgency and involvement, frames the following proposition as a personal invitation.

claims.claim_ar: تكرار عنصر «بعض» (بَعْضُنَا بَعْضًا) كأسلوب بلاغي لتوكيد العلاقة والتماثل أو التبادل بين الأطراف، يضفي قوة بيانية على نفي اتخاذ بعضهم أرباباً.
claims.claim_en: Repetition of the element 'بَعْض' (بَعْضُنَا بَعْضًا) functions as takrar (repetition) to emphasize mutuality/reciprocity and to strengthen the denial that any among them should be taken as lords.
claims.needs_review_reason: The quoted source phrase is a similar construction ('بَعْضُها مِنْ بَعْضٍ') rather than an exact citation of the ayah's wording; the rhetorical mapping is interpretive and should be reviewed against primary tafsir sources.
claims.rhetorical_effect: intensifies the negation and highlights the absurdity of mutual lordship by echoing the same term, reinforcing the unity/egalitarian sense.

warnings: Provided source_chunks do not include explicit commentary from the requested authors (al-Jurjani, al-Sakkaki, al-Baqillani, al-Suyuti, tafsir balagha). Claims were drawn only from the supplied chunks (mostly al-Kashshaf and related pieces).

Source substrings used are generic references in the chunks (e.g., discussion of the vocative particle and a similar 'بعض...من بعض' construction) rather than explicit, dedicated commentary on S3:64; some mappings are interpretive and flagged for review.
